disagreements.topic: Does the Texas TCEQ permit halt help or hurt UIG's behind-the-meter power business? (agent_3 vs the round-1 supervisor)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor: the halt could be a tailwind for behind-the-meter (BTM) power, meaning UIG. agent_3: the September order was written to close the BTM bypass, so it hits the on-site-power data centers UIG serves. agent_1 agrees with agent_3 and cites a Bracewell alert saying islanded sites are covered.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3 is right, and round 1 was wrong on this point. The 2026-09-21 order applies to every data-center permit TCEQ handles, including air permits for co-located and islanded BTM generation. The Texas Tribune reports its purpose was to stop BTM developers from avoiding the ERCOT audit. Inside Texas, then, BTM projects are delayed as well, at least until the ERCOT audit ends (expected mid-December 2026; TCEQ report due 2026-10-19). Outside Texas, grid-interconnection shortages still favor on-site power, so the UIG thesis is not broken. But the Texas freeze does not offset itself through UIG. This leaves a slightly heavier left-middle with nothing to cancel it. Agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 already price that in their revised ladders, so no further ladder change is needed.
disagreements.evidence: Texas Tribune 2026-09-21 ('Abbott's latest order appears to address concerns that data center developers who build behind the meter ... would not be delayed by the ERCOT audit'); Bracewell alert ('applies to all data center projects regardless of whether they use ERCOT grid power, including fully islanded facilities'; air permits for co-located/BTM generation affected; pause until mid-December 2026).

disagreements.topic: Is Goldman's hyperscaler capex path (+~100% 2026, +54% 2027, +12% 2028) confirmed? (agent_5 vs the round-1 supervisor)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor discounted the figure as a single X post. agent_5 says a TechFlow summary of the Goldman report and Bloomberg/Seeking Alpha coverage confirm it. agent_5 uses the 2028 +12% to shade FY28 EPS to ~$11.00 and the '32x to 22x median AI-infra de-rating' to cut its multiple to 24x.
disagreements.resolution: agent_5 is right that the figures are Goldman's, not something the X poster made up: capex of $800B (2026), $1.2T (2027) and $1.4T (2028), with growth of ~100% -> 54% -> 12%. The TechFlow summary of the report states this, and Bloomberg's headline ('rising 50% to $1.2 trillion') matches the 2027 figure. These reports are not independent originals, though: all of them trace to one Goldman note. That settles the attribution. It does not make the path correct. The note is also not bearish on levels: Goldman puts 2027 above consensus, so it supports Vertiv's FY27 more than it hurts it. The 2028 slowdown is a real second-derivative risk for multiples at the horizon, and it is mostly priced by the ~24.5x NTM multiple the agents use. I accept the path as Goldman's forecast and take the discount off. It is still one sell-side view and does not justify a further EPS cut below consensus.
disagreements.evidence: TechFlow summary of the Goldman report (2026-09-28): '$800 billion in 2026, $1.2 trillion in 2027, and $1.4 trillion in 2028 ... nearly 100% in 2026 to 54% in 2027 ... 12% in 2028', median AI-infra forward P/E 32x (Apr 2026) -> 22x; Bloomberg 2026-09-25 headline; briefs.co and AGTP recaps. All trace to one original, the Goldman note.

disagreements.resolution: Not confirmed, and not used. Twelve Data's latest bar is 2026-09-28: open $253.23, low $242.52, close $244.04, -3.65% vs $253.28 on 9/25. It shows no 9/29 session yet. The AAII page body did not load, so neither the price basis nor the cause is visible, and the -7.41% matches no single day or rolling window in the recent closes (5 sessions from 9/21 is -2.7%). Treat it as unverified context. If VRT really is ~7% lower (~$226), the stock would sit below the forecasters' median and closer to the left-middle. The forecast stays anchored to the fixed $244.04 close.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data VRT daily series and quote (last bar 2026-09-28); AAII headline 2026-09-29 (body not available).

The 2028 Goldman slowdown justifies FY28 of ~$11.0 rather than the $11.19 aggregator, which gives NTM ~$10.54. On that EPS, 24.5x (between agent_5's 24x and the others' 25x, below ETN 26.8x and NVT 24.8x FY27, above the 22x AI-infra median) gives ~$258 on P/E. The deposit-normalized FCF legs ($240-255) support this rather than lowering it much. Fair value ~$258, slightly above the mean.

disagreements.resolution: Keep ~$155: ~17x FY27 consensus and ~14.7x horizon NTM. That is well below every peer multiple and the 22x AI-infra median, and just above the verified 52-week low of $141.40 (Twelve Data). agent_4 argues $155 can be reached on sentiment alone. That is fair given 66% vol, so the break should be confirmed on a closing basis together with fundamental signals, not intraday.

confidence_reason: Both disputes are settled, but neither moves the center. agent_3's Texas/UIG correction removes an offset I had suggested in round 1, and the revised agents already price it. agent_5's Goldman path is confirmed as Goldman's and is level-positive for 2027 and rate-negative for 2028, which roughly nets out. The revised mean already includes all the round-1 corrections. My only ladder change is a small lift to the far right tail, where agent_3 is still below a 66%-vol lognormal. That is not a settled disagreement that clearly matters, so the mean should stand.
thesis_break_reason: $155 is ~17x FY27 consensus of $9.16 and ~14.7x horizon NTM (~$10.54), far below ETN (26.8x), NVT (24.8x) and Goldman's 22x AI-infrastructure median, and just above the $141.40 52-week low. A weekly close below it together with any of the following means earnings are falling, not a timing slip or sentiment: a second revenue shortfall called 'timing' at the late-October Q3 print, deferred revenue falling from $3.63B without a revenue step-up, FY27 guidance below ~$8.5, the Texas halt (now known to cover behind-the-meter sites) running past the ERCOT audit or copied by other states, or hyperscalers guiding 2027 capex below Goldman's $1.2T path.
key_drivers: Earnings keep rising while the multiple falls. FY27 consensus is $9.16 (up from $8.80 in 90 days) and horizon NTM EPS is ~$10.5-10.7. At 24.5x that is ~$258, only ~6% above $244. VRT (26.6x FY27) trades in line with ETN and NVT, not at a premium.

The capex path is Goldman's own and belongs to one sell-side house: +54% to $1.2T in 2027 (above consensus), then only +12% to $1.4T in 2028. The 2028 slowdown is the main reason the horizon multiple should stay near 24-25x rather than re-rate.

Texas permit halt (from 2026-09-21; TCEQ report 2026-10-19; ERCOT audit mid-Dec 2026) covers behind-the-meter and islanded sites, so it delays UIG's on-site-power market in Texas instead of helping it.

Visibility is low. No orders or backlog have been disclosed since Q4 2025 ($15.0B), and ~70% of the 2026 FCF guide is customer-deposit build (10-Q). The late-October Q3 print, where consensus of $1.83 is at the top of the guide, is the next test.
Realized vol is ~66% and beta near 2, so the distribution stays very wide: ~16% chance of <$146 and ~15% chance of >$427.

fair_value.reason: NTM adjusted EPS at 2027-09-28 = 0.25 x FY27 consensus $9.16 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$11.00 (the $11.19 aggregator shaded for Goldman's +12% 2028 capex growth) = ~$10.54. At 24.5x (below ETN 26.8x and NVT 24.8x FY27, above the 22x AI-infra median) that is ~$258. Diluted shares ~393M. Horizon net cash ~+$0.3B after UIG (~$1/share), which is immaterial. The deposit-normalized FCF-yield legs ($240-255) cross-check within ~7%. This is $3 above the agents' mean of $255.2, mainly because I reverse agent_3's unsupported FY27 haircut.

summary: VRT at $244 is 26.6x FY27 consensus ($9.16, still rising), in line with Eaton and nVent. My reconciled fair value is ~$258 (24.5x a ~$10.5 horizon NTM EPS), only ~6% upside with a 66%-vol distribution, and I keep the forecasters' mean ladder apart from a slightly fatter far-right tail. The second round settled two points. The Texas permit halt also covers behind-the-meter sites, so it hurts UIG's Texas market rather than helping it. The 100% -> 54% -> 12% capex path is Goldman's own (one note, bullish on 2027 levels, slowing in 2028). An unverified AAII headline suggests a ~7% drop on 9/29; Twelve Data shows only -3.65% on 9/28, and the forecast stays at the $244.04 close.
